kept.spine: The City Council gets what it asks for more often than not, and the refusals are few enough that the hall's clerks can name them.
Rundgate credits the City Council with the good years whether or not the council earned them, and at the taverns they say the good years are the whole of the case.
Who answers for the town is settled at the hall, and what comes back from the hall is not.
The criminal trade here holds a street or fills a purse, and nobody puts a finer name on it than that.
What the City Council watches is the town's own temper, and a council here falls to unrest and not to a rival.

kept.spine: A traveller who calls the City Council by any other title is corrected politely and at once by whoever is nearest.
Everyone who wants what the City Council holds is outweighed by it, and the outweighing takes work.
